title: Evidence-based circuit gate with per-tenant degradation budgeting and safe fallbacks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We need a robust mechanism to short-circuit problematic dependency paths (models, external feature services, third-party APIs) without causing cascading outages or large SLO regressions for customers. Existing coarse breaker heuristics (percent error rate or raw latency spikes) are too noisy for our heterogeneous workload mix and can either open gates unnecessarily or fail to protect downstream systems.

Proposal summary: Implement an evidence-based circuit gate that accumulates per-request signals into a weighted evidence score. Each dependency is evaluated by a sliding-window evidence accumulator; when the aggregator crosses a configurable policy threshold the gate transitions to OPEN for that dependency/region/tenant (scoped by our policy). In place of an outright block, the gate leverages a per-tenant degradation budget: tenants with remaining budget can be routed to degraded paths (cached responses, smaller quantized models, or best-effort queueing) while preserving core availability for high-priority customers. The system will also support confidence-weighted probes and region-aware slow re-open probing to validate recovery.

Key behaviors and innovations:
- Request-level evidence: combine signals such as RPC error classes (5xx vs 4xx), tail latency percentiles, model-confidence delta, and model output validation failures into a normalized evidence score per request.
- Weighted aggregation: apply configurable weights per signal type and per dependency (e.g., LLM decode anomalies carry higher weight than soft latencies). Evidence stored in an exponential decay window to favor recent regressions.
- Degradation budget (per-tenant, per-model): each tenant has a small, configurable budget (requests/minute or tokens/minute) that allows controlled use of degraded paths when gates open. Budgets are refilled over time and visible in the Console.
- Graceful fallback catalog: prioritized fallback strategies for each dependency ordered by quality/cost (cache lookup, quantized-model-1, evidence-limited retry, enqueue-with-callback). Fallbacks are pluggable and declared in dependency metadata.
- Confidence-weighted probe: during OPEN state the gate schedules low-rate probes that use a confidence floor (e.g., only allow probes if model confidence > X or if probe uses a production-validated fallback). Successful probes reduce the evidence score faster (accelerated recovery) and restore normal routing.
- Multi-region awareness: evidence aggregation is region-local by default. If region-level evidence exceeds a regional-policy threshold, a cross-region flag is set and remote regions can optionally increase local probe rate or apply cross-region short-circuits depending on policy and data locality requirements.
- Observability and auditability: every gate decision is logged with evidence breakdown, degraded-path chosen, tenant budget consumed, and a linkable trace ID for Console and Grafana. A daily synthesis report will highlight all gates opened and customer impact.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement a new UI for budget management (Console work is tracked separately). It also does not replace existing global circuit mechanisms; the evidence gate is intended to complement them and be configurable per dependency.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy signal weights create oscillation. Mitigation: start with conservative weights, 30s-2m decay windows, and implement hysteresis (min-open-duration and min-closed-duration) and probe backoff.
- Risk: budget exhaustion for heavy-traffic tenants causing degraded UX. Mitigation: expose meter and budget usage to tenants, and implement priority tiers (high-priority tenants can be excluded from automatic degradation by policy).

References:
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Evidence-Driven+Circuit+Gates
- Implementation draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421
- Dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/evidence-circuit-gates
- Example fallback policy spec: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1ExampleFallbackSpec
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes per-dependency evidence accumulator with configurable signal weights and decay window
Gate transitions to OPEN when evidence score exceeds configured threshold and logs full evidence breakdown and tenant budget usage
Console/Grafana panels show open/closed state, evidence score timeseries, and budget consumption for at least one test tenant
Fallback plumbing supports at least three fallback strategies (cache, quantized-model, enqueue-with-callback) and chooses the highest-priority available path when budget allows
Cross-region probe behavior implemented: region-local OPEN does not immediately force global OPEN; remote regions can opt into increased probe rates per policy
E2E tests simulate noisy signal injection and verify hysteresis prevents oscillation and that probes enable recovery without manual intervention
tasks: Design protobuf for evidence event and per-dependency policy (runtime + routing)
Implement evidence accumulator and weight config in runtime core
Integrate tenant degradation budget store (Redis-backed) and Console meters
Wire fallback catalog to request router and implement fallback selection logic
Add region-aware probe scheduler and confidence checks
Add logging/tracing fields and Grafana dashboards
Create e2e test harness that can drive signal noise and assert safety properties
Run canary on staging with two test tenants (low/critical) and measure SLO impact
design_decisions: Use additive evidence score normalized to [0,1] rather than counting discrete failures to support mixed-signal fusion
Scope primary aggregator per-region and per-dependency to avoid unnecessary global propagation
Implement budget as a token-bucket (tokens=degraded requests) with admin override for priority tenants
Probe requests will be counted against a separate probe budget to avoid consuming degradation budget during recovery
Fallback strategies are declared in dependency metadata to allow safe opt-in without code changes
